messages:
pagerduty-bot: P1 - GPU pool: rapid queue growth + autoscaler failed to recover (region-us-west-2). Alert: queue_length > 40k, tail latency > 1500ms. Paging oncall: @sanjay (oncall)

sanjay: I’m on it. seeing huge enqueue on gpu-serve-prod. Autoscaler logs show hitting max_replicas.

maria: can you paste the autoscaler error?

sanjay: here, from autoscaler service: `scale up failed: reached scale_limit (max_replicas=120)`. Also scheduler logs: `placement failed: no compatible node: MIG size mismatch / fragmented GPU capacity`

aj: oh that MIG sizing again. customers switched to a bunch of smaller models => fragmenting pools.

elaine: which pools are affected?

sanjay: `gpu-pool-3` and `gpu-pool-6` mainly. `gpu-pool-3` has ~28 stranded MIG slices across hosts; allocatable shows slack but not in the right slice sizes.

ops-bot: quick snapshot: queue: 42,300 reqs; active pods: 1,015; pending pods: 3,200; blocked_by: MIG_SIZE

kyle: impact? any customers in erroring state?

support-lead: support picking up increased 5xx and latency alerts. A few paying customers on Dedicated seeing timeouts ~ 20% of requests. Ticket #INC-7892 opened and flags as P1 customer impact.

maria: can we temporarily raise scale_limit to get more pods scheduled? risk: will oversubscribe and increase tail latency, but buys time.

aj: raising max_replicas won't help if scheduler can't binpack due to incompatible MIG slices. We need either repack or create smaller model workers that fit the available slices.

sanjay: quick mitigation plan: 1) emergency repack job to regroup MIG sizes (reallocate VMs) 2) temporary LIFO drain of low-priority queues 3) allow controlled oversubscribe on gpu-pool-3 with placement fallback to cpu-fallback for non-critical customers 4) contact infra to provision hot spare nodes if repack fails

elaine: steps to run repack? is it disruptive?

aj: repack = live eviction + re-create with targeted MIG sizing. We can do rolling repack to avoid full outage but will evict in-flight requests briefly. Expect small blips.

sanjay: running targeted diagnostics first. pasted scheduler snippet: ```
I0309 03:40:12 scheduler.go:412] Placement attempt failed for batch 8872
error: incompatible-slice: requested MIGs {1g.10gb x2} available {7g.80gb x1, 3g.40gb x3}
```

maria: that makes sense. a bunch of pods asking for 1g.10gb slices and only large slices left.

ops-bot: current autoscaler config snapshot: `min_replicas=100 max_replicas=120 target_util=0.65`

kyle: if we bump max_replicas to 180 can scheduler place more by spreading to other pools? maybe but risk of future fragmentation.

sanjay: I’m going to run a targeted pack plan on `gpu-pool-3`. @aj please stand by to run repack if diagnostics confirm frag.

aj: standing by. also prepare the emergency config to route lower-tier customers to cpu-fallback. Support-lead, prepare customer comms for affected customers.

support-lead: on it. drafting outage note + mitigations.

sanjay: diagnostic results: disk of nodes ok, network ok. packing plan shows 24 nodes with mixed MIG sizes, 18 of which have leftover 3g.40gb slices that could be split but need re-sizing. Repack estimate: ~40-50 nodes touched, ~3-5 minute evictions per node. Queue should start draining after ~12 minutes post-repack begins.

maria: sounds acceptable. assign rollback plan?

aj: rollback: abort repack job, re-create original node pools from snapshot. Also we can set `autoscaler.pause=true` during repack to avoid churn.

sanjay: initiating repack on subset: `rpackctl start --pool gpu-pool-3 --strategy rolling --concurrency 4 --max-evict 2`

ops-bot: repack job queued: job_id rp-20260309-51, concurrency 4, estimate 45m.

kyle: we should also open a temporary emergency scale bucket in us-west-2 (hot-spare) — infra, please spin nv4a-large-spot x8 as hot-spare.

aj: spinning up hot-spare now. command: ```
infractl request node --region us-west-2 --type nv4a-large --count 8 --purpose emergency-hotspare
```

infra / system: node request accepted. provisioning started. ETA ~7m.

maria: set safe-route: for non-paying or best-effort requests we add: `route: cpu-fallback` in routing layer for 10% of traffic. config: ```
routes.put('/infer', {fallback_percent: 10, priority: 'best-effort'})
```

support-lead: comms draft: "We are actively mitigating a GPU placement issue causing increased latency and intermittent errors for some customers in US-West. Expected mitigation within 30-60 minutes. Ticket INC-7892. Contact support for urgent cases."

sanjay: repack started on subset nodes. earliest evictions happening. monitoring queue in real-time.

ops-bot: repack progress: 6/24 nodes done. queue dipped to 31,800. pending pods reduced to 1,900.

kyle: hot-spare nodes reported ready. attaching to `gpu-pool-3` now, starting node-join.

aj: joining nodes. scheduler is now able to place an extra ~220 pods on new nodes. queue down to 18,600.

maria: great. are we seeing any errors from repack (OOM / kernel panics)?

sanjay: so far clean. one pod restart observed, auto-retry handled. latency tail calming for canaries.

ops-bot: repack progress: 18/24 nodes done. queue 8,900. pending 320.

support-lead: customers notified. two customers replied asking for ETA — responded with 45m.

aj: repack finishing. final step is to run binpack verification: `binpack-check --pool gpu-pool-3 --verify` output: `ok: 0 stranded MIG slices`

sanjay: great. autoscaler unpaused. leave max_replicas at 160 for 2 hours to allow smoothing.

maria: we should add longer-term fixes: 1) migrate some workloads to mixed-MIG deployments 2) update autoscaler to consider MIG fragmentation when deciding scale limits 3) add automated repack trigger when stranded capacity > X

aj: agree. filing follow-up RFC. I'll own autoscaler change. sanjay, can you file ops runbook updates?

sanjay: filing runbook PR now. linking here: https://redwood.internal/runs/PR-1234 (placeholder)

ops-bot: incident state: mitigated -> partial-resolved. queue back to baseline, tail latency normalized for paying customers. Keep monitoring for 2h.

support-lead: updating ticket INC-7892 to "mitigated" and adding customer notes.

maria: handoff: @aj will be the post-incident owner for follow-ups, and @sanjay handles runbook + cleanup. I’m leaving for next meeting.

aj: ack. I'll schedule the postmortem and timeline. please include guidance on MIG sizing and placement heuristics.

kyle: thumbs up. thanks everyone.

pagerduty-bot: Incident update: Incident 5177772222 marked PARTIAL_RESOLVE by sanjay at 2026-03-09T03:55:00Z. On-call handoff to aj at 2026-03-09T04:05:00Z.

sanjay: logging final notes: root cause = fragmentation from mixed workload demand causing MIG-size mismatch + autoscaler limit preventing further scale; mitigation = emergency repack + hot-spare nodes + temporary fallback routing. Follow-ups: autoscaler enhancement, automated repack trigger, customer segregation for quotas.

ops-bot: closing thread for active paging. monitor channel for regressions.
